messages:
elaine: FYI customer on prod is seeing truncated SSE events when requests traverse our gRPC->http1 gateway. They get partial JSON payloads, then a client reconnect that duplicates a few tokens billed.

sam: Can you paste a minimal example of the SSE lines they receive vs expected? Also which gateway (gRPC-web or Envoy) is in the path?

elaine: Quick paste from customer:

  expected:
  data: {\"id\":1234,\"msg\":\"done\"}
  
  observed (final chunk):
  data: {\"id\":1234,\"m

  so final bytes are cut mid-json. Client sees event end after reconnect and processes partial payload.

mike: Which HTTP versions were used end-to-end? h2 client -> h2 gateway -> h1 backend?

elaine: Client shows HTTP/2 to our edge. Gateway is translating to HTTP/1.1 for the backend. Customer repro was through a gRPC-web proxy (k8s sidecar).

jules: Likely chunk reassembly issue. Some intermediaries glue small chunks into a single TCP write, others split at different boundaries. SSE consumers expect newlines as event separators; if a proxy coalesces or truncates at RST that can leave mid-line.

sam: Any RST_STREAM or connection-level resets in the logs? That would indicate gateway is canceling streams.

elaine: From our edge trace:
  [edge] -> upstream: RST_STREAM (code=0x8) after ~14s idle
  upstream logs show 502 then a restart of the same request path.

mike: That aligns with an idle/timeout policy on the gateway killing long-lived h1 connections. When it tears down it sometimes leaves the last segment partial. We should check if gateway sets Content-Length (bad) vs Transfer-Encoding: chunked.

jules: Repro suggestion for support to share with customer: use curl --http2 -N to keep wire visible, and nghttp to inspect frame boundaries. Example:

  curl -v --http2 -N "https://edge.example.com/v1/stream?session=abc" > out.txt

  nghttp -v -n https://edge.example.com/v1/stream

elaine: Customer ran curl --http2 and saw the same, attached hex dump showing a mid-line cut and immediate FIN.

sam: Okay, action items: 1) ask customer for tcpdump/nghttp capture, 2) capture gateway proxy logs + envoy x-envoy-upstream-rq-timeout, 3) spool a temporary route to bypass gateway and confirm whether backend->client path is safe.

mike: I'll add a small server-side repro using a toy endpoint that emits SSE with ~16B payloads at 500ms intervals. If bypassed path works fine, blame gateway translation.

elaine: Also customer flagged that billing counted tokens twice when reconnect occurs. Could be because the reconnect restarts the same request and we didn't dedupe on idempotency header.

jules: We should verify token attribution: check request ids in access logs. If reconnect is a new request id, it's billed separately. Consider adding optional dedupe window keyed by session-id + last-event-id.

infra-bot: @channel seeding a debug capture: https://redwood-internal/logs/trace/2155012345 (obfuscated). Collecting samples from edge and gateway.

sam: Thanks. If gateway is confirmed culprit, escalate to partnerships (gateway vendor) for a patch; short-term: config changes to extend keepalive/idle timeout and prefer transfer-encoding chunked, not content-length. Also warn customers to use `Last-Event-ID` semantics if possible.

elaine: I'll follow up with customer with repro commands and ask for tcpdump. Marking this thread for escalation if bypass repro fails. :white_check_mark:
